tagline.en: Let AI operate your phone, hands-free
tagline.he: נותנים ל-AI להפעיל את הטלפון, בלי ידיים

description.en: Touchless connects AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini to your Android phone over MCP. The AI can open apps, read the screen, tap and type, send messages, build automations and run whole tasks for you, while you decide what it is allowed to do.
description.he: Touchless מחברת עוזרי AI כמו Claude, ChatGPT ו-Gemini לטלפון האנדרואיד שלכם דרך MCP. ה-AI יכול לפתוח אפליקציות, לקרוא את המסך, להקיש ולהקליד, לשלוח הודעות, לבנות אוטומציות ולבצע משימות שלמות בשבילכם, ואתם קובעים מה מותר לו.

release.name: Wallify 0.8.6
release.notes:
- From 0.8.6: the switch at the top of the feed reads **Live · Smart · Photos** - Smart is in the middle.
- From 0.8.5: **the place wallpapers are alive.** Around Me, Signpost, Local Line and My Street were drawn once a
  minute and did not answer the phone at all - fixed. They now turn with the phone (the map and the arrows point
  the real way; the signpost's boards turn on their pole, narrow when they point straight ahead), lean with it
  (the street sign hangs and swings, the boards sway, the map has depth) and move by themselves (a ring going out
  from where you are that lights each place it passes, a light running down the line, boards stirring in the
  wind). *Turn with the phone* is on by default, and a new *Motion* switch stills a scene for those who prefer it.
  Following the phone is drawn smoothly only while the phone is being moved.
- From 0.8.4: **four more wallpapers of where you are, and a range you choose** (47 in all). **Around Me**: a map
  of what is round you under a night sky - each town where it really lies, its dot as big as the town. **Signpost**:
  a crossroads signpost under the real sky of the hour, a board for each place pointing its way, with distance and
  direction. **Local Line**: your place as the first station of a line, the places round you its stops, each with
  an arrow and how far. **My Street**: the street you are on as a street sign, and the streets round it on a map.
  All of them and City Radar have a *Range* in Customize - 500 m, 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 or 250 km: only what is
  inside it is shown, and the wider it is the more there is. Up to 2 km they show streets (with *Precise location*;
  the phone now learns the streets up to two kilometres round you, while Wallify is open), beyond that towns - or
  choose with *Show*. A scene that has nothing in its range, or needs your precise place for streets, says so.
  City Radar and the maps can be kept north-up (*Turn with the phone* off). Distances in Hebrew are written in
  Hebrew.
- From 0.8.3: **City Radar shows what is really near.** Instead of the world's capitals it now shows the towns
  round you - from Netivot: Ofakim, Sderot, Rahat, Beersheba, Kiryat Gat, Ashkelon - each where it lies and how far,
  with the distance of the outer ring written on it. *Show* in Customize chooses: *Towns nearby* (the default),
  *Towns and villages*, *Big cities*, *Streets nearby* or *World cities* as before; *My country only* (on) keeps to
  the country you are in. Names are in Hebrew for places in Israel when the wallpaper is in Hebrew. With *Precise
  location* it also writes the street you are on, and *Streets nearby* puts the streets around you on the radar, in
  metres. The 162,000 towns are inside the app (GeoNames, CC BY 4.0), so finding them uses no network; street names
  come from the phone's own location service, asked only while Wallify is open.
- From 0.8.2: **the day outside, on your wallpaper** - six more (43 in all), in *Sky & weather*. **Horizon**: the
  sun rising and setting over the sea where it really is, its light lying on the water, the moon at night.
  **Day and Night**: the whole day as a ring in the colours the sky has at each hour, with today's real sunrise and
  sunset and the sun or moon riding it. **Window**: when it rains where you are, drops stand on the glass and run
  down it - wipe them with a finger; city lights glow behind it at night. **Today Outside**: hills, pines and grass
  under the real sky - rain, snow on the hills, grass bending in the wind, birds on a fair day. **Puddle**: rain
  rings on still water. **Thermometer**: a glass thermometer with the real temperature.
  *Window* and *Puddle* have a switch for drops in any weather.
- From 0.8.1: **13 more smart wallpapers** (37 in all). *Liquid and playful*: Day Tank (the day draining away),
  Storage Tank, Lava Lamp, Hourglass, Bubbles, Moonlit Sea, Fireflies. *Places*: City Radar (the nearest cities in
  their true direction and distance), Far Away (the way and the distance to a city you miss), Globe, Golden Hour
  (where the sun is, and when the light turns golden). *Calendar*: My Week, Countdown to a day you choose.
- From 0.8.1: **your precise place** - a wallpaper that shows a place can use the phone's own location instead of
  the city of your network: choose *Precise location (GPS)* in Customize. Wallify asks for the permission only
  then, reads the place only while Wallify itself is open, and the wallpaper uses what it last saw - it never
  follows you in the background. For the weather the point is sent rounded to about a kilometre.
- From 0.8.1: **take parts off** - switches in Customize hide parts of a wallpaper: the Cockpit's battery dial, its
  gauges, its digital clock; the Liquid Battery's number and status; clocks, coordinates and more.
- From 0.8.1: **more to touch** - bubbles burst from under a finger, fireflies and lava gather to it, water ripples.
  The Liquid Battery says how long until it is full. *This Month* can mark the days that have events.
- **Smart wallpapers** - a third side of the switch at the top of Home: *Live · Photos · Smart*. A smart wallpaper is
  drawn on the phone from its real time and state: a clock that tells the time, a tank as full as the battery, the
  sky as it is now. What you browse is the wallpaper itself, running on your phone.
- **24 of them** at first, in five groups. *Clocks*: Cockpit, Word Clock (the time in words, in Hebrew too), Orbit, Neon,
  Synthwave, Time Rings, Classic, Big Time, This Month, Year in Dots. *Sky & weather*: Weather Now (the real sky with
  drifting clouds, rain, snow, lightning, fog), Forecast, Sky Now, Daylight (the sun's path, sunrise and sunset),
  Aurora, Tonight's Moon. *Calendar*: My Day, Next Up, Day Planner. *Places*: Earth Now (a world map lit where it is
  day), Compass, World Time. *Device*: Liquid Battery (leans with the phone, bubbles while charging), Device HUD.
- **Make it yours** - *Customize* gives each wallpaper the op

release.name: TrustAPK 1.8.1070
release.notes:
TrustAPK 1.8.1070 (build 2070)

Live traffic: reuse built rows when scrolling back (#21)

Every getView built a whole row (a dozen views) even when scrolling back
to a row the list had just shown. The adapter now keeps the rows built
for the current data and gives one back when the list hands it in as the
recycled view for the same position; any notifyDataSetChanged clears them,
so a changed row is always rebuilt. A reused swipe row is snapped shut.

release.name: v3.3.1
release.notes:
## What's new

**No more "Screen offline" notifications**
Gallery Wall no longer checks the screen in the background or notifies you when it goes offline or comes back. After updating, the old check stops and its "Screen status" notification category is removed.

release.name: WatchIPTV 1.0.1
release.notes:
WatchIPTV 1.0.1 for phone, Android TV and Wear OS.

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `WatchIPTV-phone-v1.0.1-26634011.apk` | phone (Android 8.0+) |
| `WatchIPTV-tv-v1.0.1-26634011.apk` | Android TV (Android 8.0+) |

The files named without a version (`WatchIPTV-phone.apk`, `WatchIPTV-tv.apk`, `WatchIPTV-watch.apk`) are the same ones, for always-latest links.

release.name: Touchless Bridge 1.1.22
release.notes:
**Installing over 1.1.21 or older: remove the old app first, once.** This version is signed with a new key, so
Android won't install it on top of an older copy ("App not installed"). Uninstall Touchless Bridge, install
1.1.22, then connect the phone and sign in to HackerAI again. Later versions update in place as before.

A new look, an easier start, a new icon, and the app now shows when HackerAI is working.

- **You can see HackerAI working.** While HackerAI works in the chat, the app's icon in the status bar moves, and
  the notification says "HackerAI is working" with the step it is on right now ("Thinking...", "Opening Maps",
  "Phone tool: get battery status", "Running a command: nmap") and a running clock. Opened, it lists the last few
  steps. Home shows the same line. It keeps following after you close the chat window, and goes quiet when
  HackerAI is done. Only a short line per step is shown, never a command's arguments or its output.
- **The chat stays where you left it.** Closing the chat window no longer throws the page away: open it again and
  it is there at once, also in the middle of a task. A chat left idle for 10 minutes is let go and loads fresh.
- **`touchless … --say "…"` and `--done` work on the phone too** (when the phone itself is the HackerAI machine),
  as they do on a computer. The setup prompt now shows the real form: `touchless call <tool> key=value`.
- **New icon.** A hooded figure whose face is a terminal prompt (`>_`). It also has a themed-icon version, and the
  "Running" notification uses it.
- **Home shows where you stand.** A status card with the phone, Touchless and HackerAI as three points on a line.
  When the phone is connected a glowing packet travels from it to Touchless, and on to HackerAI once you're signed
  in there; while the phone isn't connected nothing moves. A button takes you to HackerAI.
- **The animation shows on every phone**, also where the phone's own animations are turned off. Settings › about ›
  "Animate the status" turns it off.
- **One thing to do on Home: connect your phone.** With a Paste button, and "Open Touchless", which opens the
  Touchless app to copy your address. Once the phone is connected the card folds away and HackerAI opens by itself.
- **HackerAI in the middle of the bottom bar.** One tap from anywhere.
- **Settings in cards.** Connection, HackerAI, always on, about. A line that isn't connected takes you back to
  Home. Running the bridge on the phone itself is now one switch in the connection list, "Remote Control on this
  phone". The setup prompt can be sent again, not only copied.
- **"Check for updates" answers.** It says "No newer version found" when there is nothing newer.
- **Battery.** Settings shows when battery use is already unrestricted, and the button only when it isn't.
- **The chat shows a page loading** with a thin line along the top.
- **Back from Settings** returns to Home.

release.name: TouchKey 0.14.2
release.notes:
## TouchKey 0.14.2

- **The trigger page reads top to bottom, in three numbered parts:**
  1. **When**: what starts it.
  2. **Only if** (optional): the conditions it must meet. With none it says "Every time".
  3. **Then do**: the steps, numbered in the order they run, with "Add another step" inside the same card.
  Under them, **Try it** has "Run it now" and the recent runs (the last 3, "Show all" for more). The name is at the
  top with when the trigger last ran. The "How it works" summary is gone: the page itself is now laid out that way.
- **Notification triggers: pick from what is showing now.** The notifications on the phone right now come first,
  each with its app's icon. Tap one to use its app and words; tap one of its buttons ("Press “Mark as read”") to
  add a step that presses it. What is already taken is marked "✓ Used" / "✓ Presses …".
- **App icons fixed.** In the app picker an app could show another app's icon (Touchless with Google Photos's
  icon) after searching or scrolling. Each app now always shows its own.

release.name: Israel App Manager 1.2.0
release.notes:
- **Android TV, tablets and every other device.** The manager now appears in the Android TV / Google TV launcher and works fully with the remote. A clear frame shows where you are. It starts on the first app and returns to the app you opened, and a long page scrolls to its end. A Refresh button replaces pull-to-refresh, and the edges stay inside the TV's safe area. Keyboards and D-pads work the same way on phones, tablets and Chromebooks.
- **Any app on any device.** An app with no build for your kind of device now installs anyway, using the build made for another one: phone apps on a TV, TV apps on a phone or tablet. Its page says what it was made for. Watch apps are still offered only to watches.
- **Fewer permissions.** The manager no longer asks to see every app on the device, only the apps you can open. Its code is easy to inspect, so Google Play Protect has less reason to warn about it.
- Fixed: on an app's page, a remote or keyboard could not move from the Back button down into the page.
- **The list of apps updates without a new version of the manager.** The catalog is now published separately from the app, checked before it is used, and the last good copy is kept for when you are offline. If a newer catalog needs a newer manager, the app says so and keeps showing the list it can read.
- **Categories and screenshots.** An app can be in several categories, category names come from the catalog, and apps can show screenshots on their page.
